      <description><p>Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website</p><p>Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.</p><p>Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/28/egypt-lina-attalah-mada-masr-press-freedom-clampdown">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p><strong>Exclusive:</strong> Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety. Repeated airstrikes, said the mother of six, were pinning its population beside the rising river.</p><p>“The drones come all the time,” said the 27-year-old. “We hear them constantly. They kill animals, civilians.       <title>Brazil’s victory for the planet and democracy: seven lessons from Lula’s win</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/29/brazil-victory-planet-democracy-lessons-lula-win</link>
      <description><p>The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France</p><p></p><p>Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow.       <description><p>The Berlin-born performer had a gift for languages that took her to Hollywood, landing roles alongside Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman</p><p>Elke Sommer, the prolific German star of the Pink Panther film A Shot in the Dark, early 70s Agatha Christie adaptation And Then there Were None, and British sex comedy Carry on Behind, has died aged 85. <a href="https://www.bild.de/unterhaltung/stars-und-leute/elke-sommer-ist-tot-hollywood-star-stirbt-mit-85-jahren-6ae2fa0e21fd087fed7ee4fb?sv_campaign_id=78888&amp;sv_tax1=affiliate&amp;sv_tax2=208063&amp;sv_tax3=Skimlinks&amp;sv_tax4=usatoday.com&amp;sv_affiliate_id=78888&amp;awc=14225_1793279347_81f7cb9355ba7198187d7a616414cd4c&amp;cid=affiliate.ca.pr.aq.bp.link_gen.tx.awin.tool">Bild magazine reported</a> that Sommer died in Los Angeles of heart failure.</p><p>German-born Sommer, whose best-known film roles were in the 1960s and 70s, was one of the wave of European performers who crossed over to Hollywood and English-language cinema with considerable success, following the postwar emergence of European new wave cinema. Sommer was one of the few German actors to make waves at the time, as Hollywood made much of her bombshell image.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/29/elke-sommer-prolific-german-star-of-a-shot-in-the-dark-and-and-then-there-were-none-dies">Continue reading...</a></description>
